recipes.name: Apple and Brie Galette
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups plus 3 tbsp all purpose flour OR
6 tbsp ice water, plus more as needed
4 Pink Lady apples, peeled and cut into 1/4 inch thick slices
1 four inch brie wheel, sliced into ‘bricks’ or half a cm thick
instructions: Begin by shredding frozen Danish Creamery Butter in a food processor or a standard box grater. - 10 tbsp frozen Danish Creamery Butter

In a mixing bowl, combine butter with flour and ice water, adding more as needed until a shaggy dough forms. - 10 tbsp frozen Danish Creamery Butter - 1 ½ cups plus 3 tbsp all purpose flour OR - 210 g all purpose flour - 6 tbsp ice water plus more as needed

Press the dough into a puck, wrap in plastic wrap, and let it chill in the fridge for 30 minutes. Between 2 pieces of parchment paper placed on a baking sheet, roll it out into a 14-inch circle, and refrigerate once more. The colder you keep the dough, the flakier the final result. - For the Galette Dough
While the dough is chilling, make the filling. - For the Galette Dough - For the Apple Filling

In a large mixing bowl, combine the thinly sliced apples, brown sugar, lemon juice, zest, nutmeg, and cardamom. - 4 Pink Lady apples peeled and cut into 1/4 inch thick slices - ¼ cup brown sugar - ½ lemon juiced and zested - freshly grated nutmeg to taste - cardamom to taste
Let the apples macerate for 10 minutes before draining and reserving the juices. - For the Apple Filling

Begin by layering a foundation of brie bricks onto your 14 inch dough circle, optionally garnishing with some freshly chopped rosemary. - Galette Dough - 1 four inch brie wheel sliced into ‘bricks’ or half a cm thick - freshly chopped rosemary

Then, assemble apple slices on top of the brie in a decorative pattern (I assembled 2 concentric circles) keeping a 2-3 inch border between the apples and the edges of the dough circle. - Apple Filling - Galette Dough
Once the brie and apple filling are assembled, gently fold the edges of the dough toward the center of the filling, overlapping as necessary, and press to seal the edges. - Galette Dough

Optionally, to make folding the edges easier, use a paring knife to make alternating cuts along the edges of the dough, leaving about 10 cm between each cut. Fold these sections toward the center of the filling, overlapping as necessary, and press to seal the edges. - Galette Dough
Brush the crust with beaten egg and bake at 400°F for about 45 minutes. - Galette Dough - 1 egg beaten

Remove from the oven and brush the filling with reserved maceration juice and the crust with melted butter. Finish with a garnish of salt and a decorative sprig of rosemary. - reserved maceration juice - melted butter - salt to taste - sprig of rosemary
